fullPassage:
Living Dictionary

In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English.

With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.

questions.passage: In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster (A)[published / abandoned] "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. Most dictionaries in Webster's day (B)[dictated / described] how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English. In his dictionary, Webster broke this (C)[convention / connection] and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 1828년 노아 웹스터가 사전을 출판했다. 당시 사전들은 사용법을 지시했다. 웹스터는 이 관행을 깨뜨렸다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① published — dictated — convention
❌ ② abandoned — dictated — connection
❌ ③ published — described — connection
❌ ④ abandoned — described — convention
✅ (A) published: 사전을 출판. abandoned(포기했다)는 반대. ✅ (B) dictated: 사용법을 지시. described(묘사했다)는 웹스터의 방식. ✅ (C) convention: 관행을 깨뜨림. connection(연결)은 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: dictated(지시했다) vs described(묘사했다): 기존 사전 vs 웹스터의 접근법.

questions.passage: Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included (A)[informal / official] words in his dictionary, critics accused him of (B)[polluting / polishing] the English language. However, Webster argued that these words (C)[captured / concealed] American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 비공식적인 단어를 포함했을 때 비평가들은 영어를 오염시킨다고 비난했다. 웹스터는 그 단어들이 미국 영어의 변형을 포착했다고 주장했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① informal — polluting — captured
❌ ② official — polluting — concealed
❌ ③ informal — polishing — concealed
❌ ④ official — polishing — captured
✅ (A) informal: 비격식 단어. official(공식적인)은 비판 맥락과 불일치. ✅ (B) polluting: 오염시킴. polishing(다듬는)은 반대. ✅ (C) captured: 변형을 포착. concealed(숨김)은 반대.
det.tip: pollute(오염시키다) ↔ polish(다듬다). capture(포착하다) ↔ conceal(숨기다).

questions.passage: With the (A)[rise / decline] of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to (B)[register / restrict] English variations all over the world. Now, it is (C)[essential / unnecessary] for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 영어의 부상과 함께 세계 각지 변형을 등록하려는 움직임이 있다. 다문화 인구의 정체성을 반영하는 것이 필수적이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① rise — register — essential
❌ ② decline — register — unnecessary
❌ ③ rise — restrict — unnecessary
❌ ④ decline — restrict — essential
✅ (A) rise: 영어의 부상. decline(쇠퇴)은 반대. ✅ (B) register: 등록/기록. restrict(제한)은 반대. ✅ (C) essential: 필수적. unnecessary(불필요한)는 반대.
det.tip: rise(부상) ↔ decline(쇠퇴). register(등록) ↔ restrict(제한).

questions.passage: In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of ①<u>providing</u> America with its own version. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than ②<u>documenting</u> the way people actually used English. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and ③<u>sought</u> to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words, critics ④<u>praised</u> him of polluting the English language.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비평가들은 그를 영어를 오염시킨다고 비난했다(accused). praised(칭찬했다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①providing: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②documenting: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③sought: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④praised(칭찬했다): 원문은 accused(비난했다). 오염 맥락에서 칭찬은 반대.
det.tip: accused(비난했다) ↔ praised(칭찬했다). accuse A of B = A를 B로 비난하다.

questions.passage: Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English. In his dictionary, Webster broke this ①<u>convention</u> and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. However, Webster ②<u>argued</u> that these words captured American ③<u>variations</u> of English, ④<u>merging</u> American English from British English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 미국 영어를 영국 영어로부터 구별하는(distinguishing) 것. merging(합치는)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①convention: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②argued: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③variations: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④merging(합치는): 원문은 distinguishing(구별하는). 미국 영어의 독자성을 강조하는 맥락에서 '합치는'은 반대.
det.tip: distinguishing(구별하는) ↔ merging(합치는). distinguish A from B = A를 B로부터 구별하다.

questions.passage: With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a ①<u>movement</u> to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is ②<u>essential</u> for English dictionaries to ③<u>recognize</u> and document words and phrases that ④<u>obscure</u> the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다문화 인구의 정체성과 경험을 반영하는(reflect) 단어. obscure(흐리게 하다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①movement: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②essential: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③recognize: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④obscure(흐리게 하다): 원문은 reflect(반영하다). 정체성을 '반영'해야지 '흐리게' 해서는 안 됨.
det.tip: reflect(반영하다) ↔ obscure(흐리게 하다, 가리다).

questions.passage: In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this __________ and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 웹스터는 이 관행을 깨뜨리고 미국인이 말하는 방식을 묘사하려 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④convention: 기존의 관행/관습. broke this convention = 관행을 깨뜨렸다. ❌ ①revolution(혁명): 깨뜨리는 대상으로 어색. ❌ ②tradition(전통): 유사하나 원문은 convention. ❌ ③innovation(혁신): 깨뜨리는 대상이 아님.
det.tip: convention: 관행, 관습. break a convention = 관행을 깨뜨리다.

questions.passage: In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, __________ American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document such words.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 미국 영어를 영국 영어로부터 구별하는 것이었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②distinguishing: 미국 영어의 독자성 강조. distinguish A from B. ❌ ①combining(결합): 반대. ❌ ③eliminating(제거): 무관. ❌ ④importing(수입): 무관.
det.tip: distinguish A from B: A를 B로부터 구별하다.

questions.passage: When he included informal words, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the __________ populations who use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 영어를 사용하는 다문화 인구의 정체성과 경험을 반영해야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③multicultural: 다양한 문화의 인구. 글의 핵심. ❌ ①monolingual(단일어): 반대. ❌ ②isolated(고립된): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④diminishing(줄어드는): 무관.
det.tip: multicultural: 다문화의. 세계 영어 변형의 핵심 = 다양한 문화.

questions.passage:
Living Dictionary

In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. Most dictionaries in Webster's day <u>dictated</u> how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'dictated'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 당시 사전은 영어 사용법을 규정했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①prescribed: 규정했다, 지시했다. dictate의 동의어. ❌ ②suggested(제안했다): 강제력 없음. ❌ ③recorded(기록했다): 이것은 documenting의 동의어. ❌ ④questioned(의문을 제기했다): 무관.
det.tip: dictate = prescribe: 지시하다, 규정하다. ↔ describe(묘사하다).

questions.passage: Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and <u>sought</u> to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'sought'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 웹스터는 미국인이 말하는 방식을 묘사하려 시도했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③attempted: 시도했다. sought to = tried to. ❌ ①refused(거부했다): 반대. ❌ ②happened(우연히): 의도적 행동. ❌ ④ceased(중단했다): 반대.
det.tip: sought to = tried to = attempted to: ~하려 시도했다. seek-sought-sought.

questions.passage: When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is <u>essential</u> for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'essential'과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 다문화 인구의 정체성을 반영하는 것이 필수적이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④crucial: 결정적인, 매우 중요한. essential의 동의어. ❌ ①optional(선택적인): 반의어. ❌ ②probable(개연성 있는): 다른 의미. ❌ ③convenient(편리한): 다른 의미.
det.tip: essential = crucial = vital = indispensable: 필수적인.

questions.passage: In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. When he included <u>informal</u> words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'informal'과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 비격식적인 단어의 반의어 = 격식적인(formal).
det.analysis: ✅ ②formal: 격식적인. informal의 반의어. ❌ ①casual(캐주얼): 유사어. ❌ ③popular(인기 있는): 다른 의미. ❌ ④familiar(친숙한): 다른 의미.
det.tip: informal(비격식적인) ↔ formal(격식적인). in- = 부정 접두사.

questions.passage: When he included informal words in his dictionary, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster <u>argued</u> that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'argued'와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 웹스터는 주장했다. 반의어 = 양보했다(conceded).
det.analysis: ✅ ①conceded: 양보했다, 인정했다. argued(주장했다)와 반대. ❌ ②insisted(고집했다): 유사어. ❌ ③claimed(주장했다): 유사어. ❌ ④maintained(주장을 유지했다): 유사어.
det.tip: argued(주장했다) ↔ conceded(양보했다). concede: 상대의 말을 인정하며 물러남.

questions.passage:
(A) In 1828, Noah Webster published a dictionary with a goal of providing America with its own <u>version</u> of the English language.

(B) The latest <u>version</u> of the software includes several bug fixes and new features.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 'version'이 (A)와 (B)에서 각각 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 미국만의 영어 판본/형태. (B) 소프트웨어 최신 버전.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: (A) version = 특정 형태/판본. (B) version = 소프트웨어 버전. ❌ ①②④: 매칭 오류.
det.tip: version: ① (무엇의) 판본, 형태 ② (소프트웨어) 버전.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to charge someone with a fault or wrongdoing"

det.korean: 누군가에게 잘못이나 비행을 따지다 = 비난하다(accuse).
det.analysis: ✅ ③accuse: 비난하다. 정의와 정확히 일치. ❌ ①praise(칭찬하다): 반대. ❌ ②defend(방어하다): 반대. ❌ ④forgive(용서하다): 반대.
det.tip: accuse: 비난하다, 고발하다. accuse A of B = A를 B로 비난하다.

questions.passage: Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used. When he included informal words, critics accused him of polluting the English language. However, Webster argued that these words captured American variations.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

Water __________ (pollute) is a serious environmental issue that affects millions of people worldwide.

det.korean: 수질 오염은 심각한 환경 문제이다.
det.analysis: ✅ Water + __________ → 복합명사. pollute → pollution.
det.tip: pollute(동사: 오염시키다) → pollution(명사: 오염). -tion 접미사.

In 1828, an American lawyer and author Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version of the English language. questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

The __________ (recognize) of diverse English varieties is important for building an inclusive community.

det.korean: 다양한 영어 변종의 인정은 포용적 공동체를 만드는 데 중요하다.
det.analysis: ✅ The + __________ → 명사. recognize → recognition.
det.tip: recognize(동사: 인정하다) → recognition(명사: 인정). -ize → -ition.

questions.passage: In 1828, Noah Webster published "An American Dictionary of the English Language" with a goal of providing America with its own version. Most dictionaries in Webster's day dictated how English words should be used rather than documenting the way people actually used English in daily life. In his dictionary, Webster broke this convention and sought to describe the way Americans spoke. He included informal words that reflected how people actually communicated. When he did so, critics accused him of __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비평가들은 그가 영어를 오염시킨다고 비난했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②polluting the English language: 원문 그대로. ❌ ①improving(개선): 비난 맥락과 불일치. ❌ ③translating(번역): 무관. ❌ ④simplifying(단순화): 무관.
det.tip: pollute: 오염시키다. 비평가들은 비격식 단어 포함 = 영어 오염으로 봄.

questions.passage: Webster argued that these words captured American variations of English, distinguishing American English from British English. With the rise of English as the world's lingua franca, there has been a movement to register English variations all over the world, for example, with the creation of the Oxford Handbook of World Englishes. English is now used by diverse populations across the globe. Now, it is essential for English dictionaries to recognize and document words and phrases that reflect __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the grammar rules established by native speakers
the identities and experiences of the multicultural populations who use English
the declining popularity of regional dialects
